identity.title: Circle Bundles with PSC over Large Manifolds

problems.location: v5 p18 final paragraph of TheoremB; journal p1417; Bolotov2009 printedp24 (PDF4)
problems.claim: The null-fiber branch uses a four-dimensional classifying-map compression whose cited proof relies on an invalid relative-to-quotient homotopy identification.
hypotheses_checked: The remaining total space is a closed oriented spin4-manifold, with torsion-free3-manifold fundamental group of cd<=3.
For the challenged topological identification take n=4,pi=Z^3,Bpi=T^3; cdpi=3 and assembly hypothesis hold. This step asserts a group-space fact independently of a PSC metric.
problems.independent_proof: In X=R^3 with cubical2-skeletonA, the boundaryS^2 of a unit cube retracts fromA by radial projection about its center. Thus pi3(A) contains pi3(S^2)=Z. LES gives pi4(X,A)=pi3(A). But X/A is the wedge overZ^3 ofS^3, so pi4(X/A)=direct_sumZ/2; twice the cube Hopf relative class is nonzero and maps to0. Hence the displayed isomorphism and freeZ2[pi]-module claim on Bolotovp24 fail in precisely n=4.
problems.decisive_evidence: Explicit infinite-order relative class versus exponent-two quotient group; exact cited proof pages23-26 read and viewed.
problems.actual_impact: A core proof dependency for TheoremB null-fiber case is unresolved. Main high-dimensional existence theorem and He's nontrivial-fiber branch are not refuted.
problems.repair: Supply a verified special-bundle compression or direct4-dimensional index/geometric obstruction. Raising the dimension to5 excludes the needed case; a nonequivariant macro-dimension bound alone does not give classifying-map compression.
problems.repair_limits: No complete replacement proof here; no PSC4-manifold counterexample to TheoremB or proof that Bolotov's theorem is false. The confirmed error is in a step of the cited proof.
problems.counterevidence: Bolotov's theorem is actually stated to include n4, so no false misquotation claim. BD2010Lemma4.1 is not a verified replacement: Dranishnikov2021Remark1.2 acknowledges its gap. Relevant later RAAG theorem also n>4.

independent_acceptance.source_locations: Theorem B null-fiber conclusion, v5 p.18 and journal physical p.18/printed1417; Bolotov 2009 physical p.4/printed24.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses: The cited proof explicitly treats n>=4 and cd(pi)=n-1 with torsion-free pi and integral real assembly injectivity. pi=Z^3 with Bpi=T^3 lies in this group/dimension range. The challenged relative-to-quotient identification is a statement about these spaces and does not itself assume a PSC manifold.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Let A be the cubical two-skeleton in X=R^3. Radial projection from a cube center retracts A onto that cube's S^2 boundary; hence pi_3(A) contains an infinite-order Hopf class. The pair sequence identifies pi_4(X,A) with pi_3(A). Collapsing A gives a wedge of S^3, whose pi_4 is a direct sum of Z/2 (cross Whitehead terms start in degree five). Twice the relative cube Hopf class is nonzero but maps to zero under suspension to the quotient. The cited isomorphism and free Z_2[pi]-module assertion are false at n=4.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Bolotov's printed theorem and proof do include dimension four; the report correctly identifies an invalid supporting proof step rather than a misquoted dimension restriction. The later KO argument detects only the suspended class and does not recover the lost element. The retained Dranishnikov remark acknowledges a different proposed replacement's gap; the later proof read here explicitly requires n>4.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency: The null-fiber branch requires classifying-map compression into Bpi^(2) to contradict Lemma 3.2. A nonequivariant macroscopic-dimension bound alone is insufficient. The spin splitting and group range do not remove the demonstrated unstable homotopy failure.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: Major proof-dependency gap in a central theorem branch; no PSC four-manifold counterexample, falsity of Theorem B, or failure of Theorem A is asserted.
independent_acceptance.repair_limits: No complete special-bundle replacement, direct index obstruction or valid dimension-four compression theorem has been verified. The nontrivial-fiber branch is outside the demonstrated gap.

problems.location: v5 p5 retraction sentence; Lemma3.1 pp12-13, intrinsic-diameter maximum; journalp1411
problems.claim: The boundary need not deformation-retract to the complement's spine; a finite list of inverse stars can have infinite intrinsic diameter.
hypotheses_checked: M=CP^3 with integral hyperplane class; Z smooth degree-k complex divisor for arbitrarily sufficiently largek, n2; canonicalEuler=kH.
W=S^1xD^3,E=S^1xS^2,K=S^1x{0}; W retracts toK and boundary inclusion induces pi1isomorphism. Constructed boundarymap PL after triangulation.
problems.independent_proof: CP^3 example has pi1E=Z/k by Lefschetz surjectivity onpi2; universalE closedoriented5-manifold hasH5=Z, impossible for3-dimensional spine. For lemma step use degree-one PLlift H with knots(0,0),(1/3,1),(2/3,0),(1,1), h_t=(1-t)x+tH(x) modulo1 and R_t(s,z)=(h_{t|z|}(s),(1-t)z). The stararc(1/4,3/8) pulls back to3separatedintervalsxS^2, so intrinsic diameter is infinite.
problems.decisive_evidence: Homology obstruction plus explicit all-hypotheses retraction and exact interval arithmetic, actually executed with Fractions.
problems.actual_impact: Literal introduction and proof step fail; same macro bound and TheoremA retained by complete replacement.
problems.repair: Use equivariant lift of finite simplicial approximation. Compact translating setsD_E,D_K and proper deck action imply only finitely many gamma with gamma f(D_E) meetingD_K; its preimage lies in finitely many translates ofD_E, hence uniformly bounded fibers. Lipschitzness follows from finite simplicial map.
problems.repair_limits: No new hypotheses, no claim the macro bound fails; compact universalE inCP^3 example has macro dimension0.
problems.counterevidence: Compactness bounds ambient distances, not the intrinsic path distance within a disconnected open star preimage. The complement, not the boundary, has the original retraction.

independent_acceptance.source_locations: Boundary retraction assertion p.5; Lemma 3.1 pp.12-13; corresponding journal p.1411.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses: A sufficiently high degree smooth hypersurface in CP^3 is an allowed n=2 divisor; Lefschetz gives pi1(Z)=0 and pi2(Z)->pi2(CP^3) surjective. Separately W=S^1 x D^3, E=S^1 x S^2 and K=S^1 satisfy both hypotheses of Lemma 3.1.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Euler evaluation kH gives pi1(E)=Z/k; its universal cover is a closed oriented five-manifold with H5=Z, so it cannot retract onto a three-dimensional complex. For the folded lift H with slopes 3,-3,3, R_t(s,z)=(h_(t|z|)(s),(1-t)z) is indeed a strong deformation retraction fixing K. The boundary preimage of (1/4,3/8) consists of (1/12,1/8), (13/24,7/12), (3/4,19/24), each times S^2, and has infinite intrinsic path diameter.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: The complement retracts; its boundary need not. A finite family of disconnected open-star inverse images does not have a finite intrinsic-diameter maximum. This does not refute the macroscopic dimension bound.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency: Theorem A uses the lemma's uniformly bounded-fiber conclusion, which admits the report's same-hypothesis replacement.
independent_acceptance.repair_verification: After finite simplicial approximation the lift is Lipschitz and equivariant for the same deck group. For compact translating sets D_E,D_K, properness makes {gamma:gamma f(D_E) meets D_K} finite; f^-1(D_K) is contained in their finite union of translates of D_E. Translation then uniformly bounds every fiber. This proves the original conclusion without a connected-star assumption.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: Minor because the complete equivariant repair preserves the lemma and Theorem A under exactly the same hypotheses.

problems.location: v5 Example10p19 final alternative; internal cross-check Example15p22; journalp1417
problems.claim: The proposed finite-cyclic fiber-image alternative at m2 cannot occur for the canonical bundles in this torus-divisor construction.
hypotheses_checked: Z2m iterated symplectic Donaldson divisor insideT2n,m>=2; canonical final-step Eulerclass e=k*j*omega.
Every sphere inZ composes to a nullhomotopic sphere inT2n.
problems.independent_proof: Euler evaluation on every a:S^2->Z is the Euler pairing k times <omega,(j a)*[S^2]>, which equals zero. This is the connecting map pi2Z->pi1S1, so it vanishes evenm2. Thus kernel fiber is0 and pi1E is always central extension1->Z->pi1E->Z2n->1, torsion-free polycyclic Hirsch2n+1.
problems.decisive_evidence: Universal Euler-pairing calculation; agrees with paper's own vanishing pullbackEuler class onp22.
problems.actual_impact: Remove unattainable branch and use asdim=vcd=2n+1 also form2; intended macro-versus-group contrast remains.
problems.repair: State infinite-cyclic extension uniformly for this canonical family.
problems.repair_limits: Does not claim a conditional assertion with impossible antecedent is logically false; does not cover arbitrary unrelated circle bundles.
problems.counterevidence: Nonzero pi2Z alone does not force nonzero Euler evaluation.

independent_acceptance.source_locations: Example 10 p.19; journal p.1417; Euler pullback calculation p.22.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses: The bundle is the canonical one from the final divisor step, with Euler class a positive integer times the restricted ambient torus symplectic class. The inclusion into T^(2n) kills every sphere because pi2(T^(2n))=0, including when m=2.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: The connecting homomorphism pi2(Z)->Z equals Euler evaluation, and <e,a_*[S^2]>=k<omega,(j a)_*[S^2]>=0 for every a. Therefore the fiber is injective in pi1(E) in every stated dimension. The resulting central extension of Z^(2n) by Z is torsion-free polycyclic of Hirsch length 2n+1.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Nonzero pi2(Z) does not imply nonzero Euler evaluation. An implication with impossible antecedent is not logically refuted; the false assertion is that the alternative can occur in this family.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency: Only the extra branch and its dimension value in Example 10 require deletion; the intended dimension contrast remains.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: Minor local example correction; use the infinite-cyclic extension and the same polycyclic dimension formulas uniformly.

hypotheses_checked: Literal unqualified statement permits n2 andM a point, a closed0-manifold.
S_r^2 carries round Riemannian metric and UW0 uses continuous maps to0-dimensional simplicial complexes.
problems.independent_proof: Every such continuous map from connectedS2 is constant. Therefore UW0(S_r^2)=diamS_r^2=pi*r>2r.
problems.decisive_evidence: Connectedness and exact round geodesic diameter.
problems.actual_impact: Only numerical introductory width bound changes; PSC scaling and macroscopic-dimension conclusion remain.

independent_acceptance.source_locations: Urysohn width definition p.2 and product projection bound p.3.
independent_acceptance.hypotheses: The written unqualified statement permits n=2 with M a point. The sphere carries its round Riemannian metric, and the target is a zero-dimensional simplicial complex.
independent_acceptance.decisive_evidence: Connectedness forces every continuous map from S_r^2 to such a target to be constant. Thus UW_0(S_r^2)=diam(S_r^2)=pi*r>2r. More generally the displayed projection's fiber diameter is pi*r.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: If n>2 were intended, the n=2 literal counterexample would be excluded, but the stated projection still proves only pi*r. Extrinsic chord diameter is not the product Riemannian distance.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency: The constant correction does not alter PSC scaling or the macroscopic-dimension conclusion.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: Minor quantitative introductory error; replace 2r by pi*r.
